proof_nl: Let x be an arbitrary real number. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is an integer satisfying floor(x) <= x. Subtracting floor(x) from both sides gives x - floor(x) >= 0. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real x. Hence, for all real x, 0 <= x - floor(x).
solver_summary: Directly from floor(x) <= x, subtract floor(x) to obtain x - floor(x) >= 0 for all real x.
